cards.title: The course of the war
body: Even though Britain and France declared war on Germany on September 3, 1939, war did not begin automatically. Until April 1940, there was almost no war in Europe. That is why WWII was
Called a “phony war” at the beginning.
The war continued with fast military invasion of Denmark, Norway, Netherlands, Belgium & France one after another one by one in 1940.

The German forces attacked France troops by the Luxemburg and the Ardennes Forest (a forest found in Southeastern Belgium). 380,000 British forces who meant to help the French army trapped in DUNKRIK and successfully evacuated with the help of the British navy and Belgian civilians on April 1940.

With the help of Mussolini Hitler occupied France on June 22 1940 and replaced a Nazi leadership in France (known as Vichy France and was led by an aged French hero of the First World War named Marshal Petain.

The USA followed the policy of isolationism, though British asked for help US citizens don’t want their country to interfere. But US sent its military and logistic aid through its lend-lease act starting from 1941.
Hitler at first wasn’t sure to attack Britain or the USSR but decide to attack Britain first on august 1940 he launched air strike on Britain using the Luftwaffe.

The British retaliated in kind and bombed German cities, even though German air force attacked civilian cities British army couldn’t be easily defeated Hitler postponed British attack and decided to attack USSR by the operation of Barbosa.

Despite their initial success, a severe winter and strong Soviet resistance stopped the Germans. In December 1941, the Soviets carried out a successful counterattack, and thereby Germany’s plan collapsed.
On December 7, 1941, Japanese airplanes attacked US naval base at Pearl Harbor in the Hawaiian Islands which pulled the entry of USA to the war on the side of allies.
The United States declared war on Japan the next day. Three days later, Hitler declared war on the United States.

The entry of the United States into the war changed the balance of power between the Allied and Axis powers. Great Britain, the United States, and Soviet Union formed a coalition known as the Grand Alliance.

Until late 1942, Germany had the upper hand in the war. Its forces in North Africa, led by the famous general Erwin Rommel, were able to break through British defenses in Egypt and advanced toward Alexandria, but with us entry the war shifted to the favor of the allies.

cards.title: The defeat of Germany (European Theatre)
body: In North Africa, British forces stopped the advancing German troops at El Alamein in the summer of 1942.
In November 1942, British and American forces invaded French colonies in North Africa and forced German and Italian troops to surrender in May 1943.
The Germans were forced to surrender at Stalingrad and the entire sixth Germany army were encircled and completely smashed by the USSR troops on 2 February 1943.

Besides the war the Nazi Germany had done some atrocities towards other so called inferior races. By building concentration camps or simply shoot them down.one good example was the HOLOCAST were about six million Jews were exterminated in different camps. The largest and most infamous of the camps was Auschwitz.

Since 1943, the Allies had been planning to invade German occupied France from Britain across the English Channel. The Allies managed to trick the Germans into believing that the invasion would come on the flat plains of northern France. Instead, Allied forces under US General Dwight Eisenhower landed on the Normandy beaches on June 6, 1944. The invasion of Normandy, also known as D-Day invasion, is considered to be the largest naval invasion in history.

The Germans used newly developed tanks in their offensive. But, they were severely defeated by the Soviets at the Battle of Kursk, fought between 5 and 12 July 1943.The Battle of Kursk was the greatest tank battle of WWII.
Hitler committed suicide on April 30, two days after Mussolini was shot by Italian resistance fighters. On May 7, 1945, Germany surrendered and WWII was finally over in Europe.

Us president H.S.Truman decided to use chemical nuclear bombs on japan on August 1945 on HIROSHIMA and three days later in NAGASAKI. These incident made japan to surrender. And WW2 officially ended with victory of allies.

cards.title: Consequences of the war
body: PoliticalConsequences: The war had many political consequences, among which were the following:
Germany, Italy and Japan were completely defeated and their totalitarian regimes were overthrown
The war weakened the economic, political and military power of Germany, Japan, Britain and France. In their place, the United States and the Soviet Union emerged as world superpowers.
The occupation of Eastern Europe by the USSR during the war led to the spread of communism in Europe.
The war led to the division of Germany into Soviet controlled East and US controlled West Germany

Rivalries among the wartime Allies emerged soon after the end of the war. These rivalries were characterized by economic, political, military and ideological struggles between the communist bloc led by the Soviet Union and the Western bloc led by the U.S.A.
The war resulted in the foundation of the United Nations Organization in 1945 to promote peace, security and international co-operation
The war also contributed to the process of decolonization in Africa and Asia by weakening the ability of European colonial powers to continue to hold onto their colonies.

cards.title: The end of Italian rule
body: With the huge army the Italians seems undefeated specially after they defeat the British arm and control Kassala, Galabat (in Sudan) and British Somali land in 1940.
Alarmed by the defeat the British soldiers led by general William Platt started counter attack and started pushing the Italians.

Before the British army started counter attack by using planes they started dropping pamphlets to the Eritrean people (Askaries were asked to give up arms or join the British army) promising them independence from the Eritrean people.
And the British army started to gain territories and in 1941 the Italians were defeated with the capture of Asmara in 1941.
The battle of Keren was one of the fiercest battles of WWII in East Africa which was fought for 12 days and ended in march 27 1941.

cards.title: British Military Administration
body: Britain occupied Eritrea on behalf of the Allied powers. It declared Eritrea an “Occupied Enemy Territory.”

Britain was obliged to govern Eritrea according to the Hague Convention of 1907. The Convention obliged Britain to: Maintain peace and order in Eritrea Maintain the economic and social life of Eritreans Respect the organization and administration of the territory
For the first three years, the British army didn’t set up an army instead they preserved the Italians in offices and further gave them additional lands.

cards.title: New developments during the British period
body: The Eritrean economy began to deteriorate. Thousands of ex-askaris were left unemployed and inflation increased.
Asmara was overpopulated and suffered from acute shortages of food, housing and basic facilities.

Eritrea also suffered from security problems. Especially in the western lowlands, extensive conflicts emerged between the Beni Amir of Eritrea and Hadendewas of Sudan. The Tigres also started their struggle for emancipation from feudal domination.
Thus, the hope that the British would bring peace, prosperity and independence to Eritrea was eroded.

cards.title: TURNING POINT
body: On 3 August 1944 one article was posted on the Eritrean Weekly News (an official weekly newspaper sponsored by the BMA) under a pen name, Hade Eritrawi or One Eritrean. That wrote about the partition of Eritrea later the writer was known it was Brigadier Stephen H. Longrigg.

It created two opposing views within the members of Mahber Fqri Hager. Some members of the association supported the idea of union with Ethiopia and some expressed their desire for an independent Eritrea. The differing opinions about the future of Eritrea split Mahber Fqri Hager into two.

In reaction to the above mentioned problems and discontents. Some Eritrean legends such as shiek Ibrahim Sultan, fitewrari Gebremesqel Weldu ,Ras Tesema asmrom ,Weldab Weldwmariam Etc.formed the Mahber fqri hager party on May 5 1941.

The association elected an executive committee of twelve members with equal number of Muslims and Christians represented. From among them, Fiewrari Gebremeskel Woldu, Abdulkadir Kebire, and Fitewrari Haregot Abbay were elected president, vice president, and general secretary respectively.
The main objectives of Mahber Fiqri Hager were to present public grievances and serve as advisory body to the British Military Administration.
The differing opinions about the future of Eritrea split Mahber Fqri Hager into two.
The Ethiopian government started to infiltrate the association using Orthodox clerk’s such one was the famous Abune Marqos who changed the association name to MAHBER FQRI HAGER ERITRA MS ETHIOPIA.
In reaction to this some prominent leaders like WEL-WEL, SHIEK IBRAHIM SULTAN, DEGIAT ALI HASSEN, AND DEGIAT ABREHA TESEMA formed the ERITREA N ERITRAWYAN party separated from Mahber fqri hager.
Even though BMA did not allow open political activities; both Eritrea for Eritreans and Association of Love for Country Eritrea with Ethiopia began to campaign for support among the Eritrean society.

lessons.title: Plans of regional and International Powers over Eritrea (1941- 1945)

cards.title: A. Ethiopia and Egypt
body: 1. Ethiopia officially presented its claim in April 1942.It demanded that Britain return Eritrea to Ethiopia. It justified its claim by arguing that Eritrea had been historically, culturally and religiously part of it. British refused.
2. Egypt In the memorandum it presented to the Paris Peace Conference in 1946, Egypt claimed Eritrea on the basis of historical and economic ties.

cards.title: B. Britain and United State
body: 1. Britain: in Somalia it had a plan to create a greater Somalia that would include British Somaliland, the former Italian Somaliland, the Ogden (a Somali region in Ethiopia), and some parts of Kenya. In Eritrea they planned to partition Eritrea into two.The western lowlands would be joined to the Sudan, and the highlands and the coastal areas would be annexed to Ethiopia.

2. US: Right after Britain took Eritrea from Italy, the United States began to use the airport at Gurae. In August 1943, the United States and Ethiopia signed an agreement of cooperation. As we will see later, the US would strongly support the Ethiopian claim over Eritrea.

lessons.title: The End of WWII and the Subsequent Economic and Political Situations in Eritrea

cards.title: I. Socio-Economic Problems and the Rise of Banditry
body: After the allied were defeated by German forces in Libya and controlled some part of Egypt British decided to replace Eritrea as industrial base to support the allied in North Africa. This consequently revived the Eritrean economy.
Therefore, from 1943 up to the end of WWII in 1945, Eritrea experienced an economic boom.

But with the end of the war in 1945 the British Military Administration began to systematically dismantle industries, port and airport facilities and transport networks built during the Italian period and along the course of WWII. Their plan was to make Eritrea look and forced UNO to decide the partition of Eritrea.

Here are some examples of the industrial and infrastructural plants dismantled and sold by the British; The US- built airport at Gurae was destroyed The railroad that was planned to be extended from Aqordet to Kassala and to Gondar was dismantled and sold to the Sudan for scrap The cable way built during the Italian period was dismantled The floating dry dock at Massawa was sold to Pakistan Sixteen harbor boats were sold to Italians and Arabs The cement factory in Massawa was sold to the Sudan Cotton, tobacco and coffee plantations were abandoned and gold mines were destroyed.

After the end of WWII in 1945, Ethiopian support and involvement were intensified. It armed the unionists and encouraged them to carry out attacks against independence supporters and foreigners. This resulted in increased armed terrorist attacks and intimidations on independence supporters all over Eritrea.
In the western lowlands of Eritrea was beset by conflicts between the Tigres and Shmagle for emancipation.

cards.title: Wa’ela Biet Gerghis (Biet Giorgis Conference)
body: In October 1946, the British Military Administration officially allowed the formation of political parties.in order to solve their differences the UNIONIST AND ERTRA N ERTRAWYAN decided to meet at BIET GERGISH in 24 November, 1946.
The main proponents of the conference were Gebremeskel Woldu of the unionist party and Woldeab Woldemariam of Eritrea for Eritreans.

The Unionists came to the meeting with armed youth to intimidate the participants. After the opening ceremony, Tedla Bairu made a speech, attacking the organizers in general and Woldeab Woldemariam in particular. Soon, the conference was disrupted without much discussion and the attempt at reconciliation failed.

cards.title: Establishment of Political Parties
body: After the BMA allowed the formation of parties on October 1946, the parties set up in order were :

Al Rabita Al Islamiya (Muslim League) : The party The League elected Said Bekri Al Murghani as president and Ibrahim Sultan as secretary general and aimed for unconditional independence and emancipation of the Tigre (end of master serf relation) founded in DEC 1946.

Unionist Party: The Unionist party was formally founded on March 21, 1947 in Asmara. Its objective was unconditional and direct union with Ethiopia. It elected Degiat Beyene Beraki as president and Tedla Bairu as secretary general. The party had an official newspaper named Ethiopia.

Eritrea for Eritreans (Liberal Progressive Party) : was established on February 18, 1947 at Adi Keih. The objectives of the party were similar to those of the Muslim League. It was opposed to union with Ethiopia and demanded for complete independence after ten years of British trusteeship. The leaders of the party were Raesi Tessema Asberom (President), Dejazmach Maasho Zeweldi (Vice-President) and Grazmatch Seyoum Maasho (Secretary General).

Pro- Italy Party: was established in July 1947. The majority of its members were ex-askaris. The main political objective of the party was Eritrean independence after 15 years of Italian trusteeship. The party elected Idris Hassen Naib and Mhanzel Tesfazgi as president and secretary, respectively. The party had an official Tigrinya newspaper named Brhan Ertra.

lessons.title: The Four Great Powers and the UN over the Future of Eritrea

cards.title: 11.6.1 The Eritrean Case under the Four Great Powers
body: After the end of WW2 the great powers (USA, USSR.FRANCE and BRITISH) meet to decide the future of Eritrea, Libya and Somalia. Their decision look as follows:

I. Britain: had a plan to partition Eritrea into two, give the western lowlands to the Sudan and annex the highlands and the coastal areas to Ethiopia. In Libya, its plan was to divide the country into two and give Tripolitania to Italy and take Cyrenaica for itself. What’s more, Britain also wanted to create Greater Somalia.

II.US: proposal varied from time to time. At first it proposed the port of Assab be given to Ethiopia and that after ten years of collective trusteeship Eritrea and Libya would be given independence. When France and the USSR rejected this proposal, the US then joined France and the USSR in accepting Italian trusteeship over Eritrea.

Since the great the great powers had to come to agreement they decided to send a commission to Eritrea to assert the wishes of the people he Four Powers Commission (FPC) arrived in Eritrea on 12 November 1947 and stayed until 3 January 1948.

FPC conducted interviews collected statements and received oral responses and report its findings to the great powers. The Four Great Powers could not reach an agreement on the future of Eritrea and the other Italian colonies. As a result, they referred the issue to the UN General Assembly on 15th September 1948.

cards.title: 11.6.2 The Eritrean Case in the United Nations
body: The Eritrean question, along with that of the other two ex-Italian colonies, was submitted to the third regular session of the General Assembly, which opened on 21 September 1948. But since the case was new to many member states. The pro-independence elected Adulkadr Kebire but he was shoot by the Unionist bandits in 1949 March 27.

The General Assembly; discussed the matter of the former Italian colonies from 5 April to 13 May 1949. In the discussion, Britain and the United States adopted a common approach to the matter. They proposed that Eritrea should be partitioned with its larger segment going to Ethiopia, Tripolitania should be granted independence, Cyrenaica should be placed under British trusteeship, and Somaliland should be allocated to Italy.
France: proposed a return of the former colonies to Italy, with the exception of the Danakil region of Eritrea to be ceded to Ethiopia.
Italy: opposed annexation or partition of Eritrea and proposed Italian trusteeship to be followed by full independence. Like France, however, Italy proposed Assab to be given to Ethiopia.
Latin American countries: supported the idea of Italian trusteeship over Eritrea and the cession of a strip of land to Ethiopia.
USSR: rejected the idea of partition or annexation of Eritrea, but supported the idea that Ethiopia should get an access to the sea through the port of Assab.

Ethiopia, for its part, repeated its claim over Eritrea on the grounds that Eritrea was economically nonviable to be independent and both the Eritrean and Ethiopian people had cultural, linguistic, religious, and historical ties. In addition, countries such as Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Philippines, Yugoslavia, and Turkey supported Eritrean independence. Representatives of Eritrean political organizations also presented their respective ideas on the future of their country. While discussion were on session Britain and Italy signed a secret agreement known as the BEVIN-SFOEZA PLAN .according to this plan Italy was to receive Tripolitania and Somaliland while Britain and France were to retain Cyrenaica and the Fezzan, respectively. The plan proposed to partition Eritrea between Ethiopia and Sudan. After the Bevin-Sforza plan disagreement erupt in the general assembly IBRAAHIM SULTAN give a strong speech saying that if Eritrea is not given its independence there would not be peace in horn Africa.

After the third session of the general assembly the INDEPENDENCE BLOCK was formed. The parties that formed the Bloc were; Muslim League, Liberal Progressive Party, New Eritrea Party, Eritrean War Veterans, Italo-Eritrean Association National Muslim Party of Massawa, Intellectual Party, The Independent Eritrean Party.
The main goals of the Bloc were; Immediate independence of Eritrea.
Establishment of a democratic government. Maintenance of Eritrea’s territorial integrity.
Prevention of partition proposed in the Bevin-Sforza plan.

British officers succeeded in splitting the Bloc in February 1950. As a result, two splinter groups, namely the Muslim League of Western Province and Liberal Unionist Party were formed. The Muslim League of Western Province was formed by splitting from the Muslim League. It was led by Ali Radai and demanded for the independence of the western province. The Liberal Unionist Party was formed by a breakaway group of former Liberal Progressive Party members led by Abraha Tessema.

cards.title: The Report of the UN Commission for Eritrea
body: The UNO commission composed of Burma, Guatemala, South Africa, Norway and Pakistan.
Pakistan and Guatemala proposed independence for Eritrea after ten years of direct UN Trusteeship.
South Africa and Burma recommended the federation of Eritrea with Ethiopia, under the sovereignty of the Ethiopian crown.
Norway proposed the unconditional union of Eritrea with Ethiopia with some limitation relating to the western province.
Thus, in December 1950, with strong pressures from the United States, the UN General Assembly passed Resolution 390A (v), which federated Eritrea with Ethiopia.

The act passed the rights of the state gov’t and federal state gov’t as follows, 1. Eritrea shall constitute an autonomous unit federated with Ethiopia under the sovereignty of the Ethiopian Crown. 2. The Eritrean government shall have legislative, executive and judicial branches

3. The Federal Government shall have jurisdiction over defense, foreign affairs, currency and finance and external and internal trade including ports, The Eritrean Government, on its part, shall have jurisdiction on internal matters

4. There shall be no barriers to the freedom of movement of persons and goods within the federal area. Customs duties on goods entering or leaving the Federation which have their final destination or origin in Eritrea shall be assigned to Eritrea.
5. An Imperial Federal Council composed of equal numbers of Eritrean and Ethiopian representatives would meet at least once.
6. A single nationality shall prevail throughout the Federation. 7. The Federal Government as well as Eritrea shall ensure residents rights to all basic fundamental rights.

But, after Resolution 390A (v) was passed; all parties called a reconciliatory meeting on December 31, 1951, and accepted the federal resolution. Independence Bloc changed its name to Eritrean Democratic Front and declared that it would fight for the maintenance of Eritrean autonomy within the federal arrangement.

cards.title: What is Federation?
body: Federation: (derived from a Latin word fidere, meaning,to trust) is a political system in which two or more states voluntarily from a union that leaves foreign affairs, defense, currency and foreign inter-state trade etc to the central (Federal) government, but retains powers of government over some internal matters. Indeed, the system Federation provides members of federal system will have equal standing or jurisdiction system.
1. Why was the Federation of Eritrea and Ethiopia not just and Fair?
2. Mention the defects of the Federation?
3. What was the task of Imperial Federal Council?
4. List the political parties represented the Eritrean Assembly in 1952?
5. Who was the first chief executive of the Eritrean Government in 1952?
Basically – Ethio- Eritrean Federation did not reflect the actual meaning of Federation; Eritrea forced to accept the Resolution 390 A(v) that federated it with Ethiopia without any alternative.

UNO, General Assembly passed a Resolution coded 390A (v) on Dec, 2, 1950 to Federation Eritrea with Ethiopia. At that time, USSR, Cuba, Guatemala, Checozslavakia, Norway and others opposed Federation Eritrea with Ethiopia, similarly USA and her allies supported and play a key role in Federating Eritrea with Ethiopia.

cards.title: THE FEDERAL ACT
body: The Federal Act consisted of seven sections (1-7) of resolutions of 390A(V) outlines the basic provisions were:
Eritrea to have autonomy (self- government) under the sovereignty of the Ethiopia crown.
The Federal government would have the power over defense, Foreign affairs, currency. Inter-state trade etc. And to levy tax to meet expense.
The Jurisdictions placed under Ethiopian government would have legislative, executive and judicial powers in domestic matters.

An Imperial Federal Council composed of equal number of Eritrean and Ethiopian representatives, would meet once a year. The council would provide advice concerning the common affairs of the federation as indicated in clause no3. Eritrean citizens would participate, in the judicial and executive branches and they would be represented by Ethiopia(Federal) government in legislative branch. Clause number 3.
The federation region would consist of one zone for customs purposes and there would not be any restrictions on the freedom movement of people and goods, coming into and out of the federal region.
The nationality would be same in the federation except for foreigners.
The federal Government as well as Eritrea would ensure the residents in Eritrea, without distinction/separation, of sex, race, language and Religion.

cards.title: Adoption of the federation by the Eritrean Assembly
body: On December 14,1950,the UN General Assembly appointed the Bolivian diplomat Dr, Anzio Mateinzo to draft a constitution and organize the Eritrean government. He arrived in Asmara on February 9,1951.The draft of the constitution was then presented to the Eritrean Assembly. It should be noted that Ethiopia and Britain had seen to it that supporters of the union would have the upper hand in the Assembly.

Towards this end they had manipulated the elections in favor of parties opposed to independence. Consequently, in the 1952 elections the Unionist and the Moslem League of Western Lowlands (which supported the partition of Eritrea) secured favorable results. Those in the 68 member Assembly, the Unionist party gained 32seats,the Muslim League of Western Lowlands got 17 seats and the DemocraticFront19seats.The parties represented in the Assembly were:
Unionist party
The democratic Front
The Moslem League of Western lowland
The Liberal Progressive Unionist Party and Hizbi al Wetani.

The Democratic Front led by Ibrahim Sultan strongly opposed the moves to weaken the Eritrean autonomy. The Democratic Front demanded that Eritrean should have its own flag, Tigrigna and Arabic to be official languages.Moreover, they stated their opposition the placement of an Imperial Representative in Eritrea. Only the first two were accepted.
Finally the draft constitution was accepted with minor changes by the first Eritrean Assembly. The draft constitution included the following provisions:
The government was to be structured in legislative, executive and judicial branches
The Chief Executive to be appointed by the Assembly
Tigrigna and Arabic were to be the official languages of Eritrea
Eritrea was to have its own flag, seal and coat of arms
An Imperial Representative to be placed with mainly ceremonial roles and limited censorship
All persons were to enjoy fundamental rights and liberties.
The constitution and Federal Act were ratified by the Ethiopian Monarch in August and September 1952 respectively. TedlaBairu, the first chief executive and head of the first Eritrean Government.
Some of the weaknesses of the federation were:
Democratic Eritrea was federated with an autocratic and feudal(monarchic) Ethiopia through imposition
The head of the Ethiopian government and the Federal Government was Emperor Hailesellassie. Therefore, there was no difference between the Ethiopian government and the Federal Government.
The placement of the Imperial Representative that was not part of the Federal Act.
The absence of an article that invites for international intervention in case of violation by one of the parties.

cards.title: FOCUS QUESTIONS
body: 1. What was the task of Matienzo in Eritrea in 1950?
2. Explain the phases for the dismantlement of the Federation?
3. What do you think that the causes for the student‟s strike and worker‟s demonstration?
4. Who replaced Tedla Bairuin1955 ?

The Federal Act was implemented on September15, 1952. As soon as the federation started, Emperor Haileselasse began a systematic violation of the constitution and dismantling of the Eritrean autonomy, because his ambition was to incorporate Eritrea as an integral part of his empire.Ethiopian foreign Minister Aklilu Habteweld complained to Anzio Mateinzo the UN Commissioner that;

Thus, Ethiopia considered Federation as only a step towards union even before, the British Adminstration transferred the state property and key sectors of the economy such as ports, railways, cable and road transport, postal and telephone services as well as salt processing plants to the Ethiopian Government.
Thus, he started to erode the federation in three consecutive phases.

cards.title: First phase 1952-1955
body: The Ethiopian government took the following measures to dismantle the federation:

It started to weaken the Eritrean economy by discouraging foreign investors and businessmen from involvement in Eritrea. It also closed some factories like SEDAO for hydro- electric power in Western Eritrea and FIAT-car industry in Dekemhare and textile industry.Others also moved them to Ethiopia.
Ethiopia banned formation of workers union but, BMA allowed for its formation in January 1952. President was Woldeab Woldemariam and deputy was Siraj Abdu.
The mouthpiece of workers union was voice of Eritrea (DehaiEritrea) Newspaper and its editor was Mohammed Salih. In 1954 the newspaper was closed and its editor was arrested.
Ethiopia and the unionists started to attack the Eritrean Labor Union and attempted to kill its president Woldeab Woldemariam.
The Imperial Federal Council was virtually dissolved in 1953.
Involvement in the appointment of ministers.

The first chief Executive of the Eritrea Government, Tedla Bairu and the president of the Assembly, Ali Mussa Redai were deposed by Emperor Hailesellassiein1955 and replaced by Asfaha Weldemicael and Idris Mohammed Adem respectively.
The imperial Representative,Andargachew Messay’s interference in the domestic affairs of Eritrea.

cards.title: Second phase 1955-1958
body: In November 1955 a new Ethiopian constitution that completely ignored special status of Eritrea was proclaimed. According to this constitution all the islands and the territorial waters of Eritrea were put under the sovereignty of the Ethiopian crown. Some of the measures taken under this period were:
The appointment of Asfaha Woldemichael who had been the vice-Imperial Representative as a Chief Executive.
Ethiopia appointed Tedla Uqbit as the head of Eritrean police in violation of the rights of the Eritrean Assembly.
All political parties except the Unionist party were banned and an undemocratic election by bribery and intimidation was held in1956.
Tigrigna and Arabic were banned as official languages of Eritrea and replaced by Amharic (1956).

cards.title: Student’s Strike
body: In 1956,Tigrigna and Arabic were banned as official languages.This caused resentment among the people.Students at Hailesilasie Secondary School in Asmara took out the streets in protest.In1957,they staged a demonstration. AsfhaWeldemichael responded by imprisoning the organizers of the strike.Despite the government crackdown,however, students were continued in many parts of Eritrea.

cards.title: Workers’s Demonstration
body: Eritrean workers staged a demonstration demanding to be recognized as a free trade unionin1958.The office of Asfha Weldemicael, ,refused to concede the reguest.Consquently workers throughout Eritrea came out on strike; soon they were joined by the general public. The confrontation culminated in brutal suppression of the strike by the government. Shots were fired against defenseless civilians as result 9 peoples were killed and 534 were wounded. Organizers of the demonstration were jailed. The strike was called off only after the government threatened to deploy Ethiopian armed forces. Once the demonstration was over, the government disbanded the labor union.

cards.title: Third phase Dismantlement 1958-1960
body: The final measures taken for the dismantlement of federation were as follows:
The removal of the Eritrea flag (Dec. 1958).
The Eritrean constitution was replaced by a new labor code (Sep. 1959)
The introduction of Amharic as language of instruction.
Change of the names of Eritrea Government and chief Executive in to Eritrea Administration and chief Administrator (1960).
Putting of Eritrean schools under the ministry of Education of Ethiopia (1960)

General Abiye Abeba replaced Anargachew Messai as Imperial Representative in 1959. He and AsfahaWoldemichael as well as Keshi Demetros Ghebremariam, the head of the Unionist party and Vice-president of the Assembly speeded up the final dismantlement of the federation.

cards.title: Formation of Eritrean Liberation Movement(ELM)
body: There was individual and mass opposition in response to Ethiopia‟s violation of the constitution and the Federal Act but was not succeded. This shows, at that time conducting arm struggle inside Eritrea was so difficult.

In the meantime the Eritrean Liberation Movement was founded by Eritrean refugees in port Sudan in November1958. Among the founding members were;Mohammed Seid Naud,Salih Ahmed Iyay, Mohammed el-Hassen,Tahir Fedab, Yassinel-Gede and others. It was clandestine movement.
The objectives of ELM was:
promoting national Unity, securing independence and to set up ademocratic government.
The E.L.M organized its members from all social groups in cells of seven. Hence, it was known as Mahber Shewatte in the highland region and Harakat Altahrir al Eritrea in the lowland.
Due to its secret nature of organization its members did not know each other except for the seven members in one cell.
Thus, there was no coordination and close linkage among the members and even with the leadership living abroad.
E.I.M had no plan of conducting armed struggle from the very beginning. It planned to overthrow the government structure. Armed struggle was only considered in case the coup d’état failed.

cards.title: Hostilities between ELM and ELF
body: The members of E.L.M were disappointed by its delay to start the armed struggle. As a result some of them withdrew and joined ELF were it had already started armed struggle on September 1, 1961 in the Barka region. Finally, ELM leaders planned to conduct armed struggle and sent fifty fighters to Sahel. Even though ELM tried to approach ELF to coordinate their struggle, ELF did not accept it. Some of their sources of conflicts were.

Finally, the supreme council of E.L.F decided to take military action against ELM thus, ELF attacked the fighters of ELM at the Battle of Ella Tsaeda in 1965. This event led to the final dismissal of the political movement of ELM.
